[LGRA.10.8] **An action's indented block.** An `emit`, `publish` or `call`
action may continue on indented lines under its head line. No other action
may: under `log`, `cache`, `cache_delete` or `withdraw` an indented block is a
syntax error, and the compiler must refuse it.

```
action_block    ::= INDENT block_line+ DEDENT

block_line      ::= action_arg+ NEWLINE                 # emit, publish, call
                 |  call_as NEWLINE                     # call only ([LGRA.10.1])
                 |  continuation                        # call only ([LCCO.2.1])
```

`action_block` follows [LGRA.10.1]'s `action` and `call_action` productions,
whose head line may carry arguments of its own.

What the productions do not say:

- Argument lines and continuations may come in any order.
- A `call` holds at most one `as`, its correlation ([LRST.1.1]): one `as` line
  in its block, or the `call_as` on its head line, and not both. After an `as`
  line the block holds only continuations ([LCRS.6.2.3]).
- **The block is layout and nothing else**, as [LGRA.6.7.4] says of `let`. The
  compiler must compile an action whose arguments are spread over block lines
  exactly as the action with the same arguments, in the order they are
  written, head line first, all on its head line; and an `as` line exactly as
  the same `as` clause at the end of the head line. Interleaving argument lines
  with continuations changes neither the arguments nor the continuations'
  order.
